units.reason: A docked station's PA names its own bare shelf or hot commodity, in the market screen's own thresholds

A wing striking colors speaks once as the falling-resolution register; the ear audit covers every landed gameplay emit again (drill charge sequence, shield pylon pair, cruise wrestle now voiced; 17 emits honestly silent)
A shoved hull's pilot breaks: a live tumble feeds the mind's fear, so a hard shove panics an undisciplined pilot mid-fight
The market why-tip attributes a price move to the player's own hand trade, cited from the economy's trade ledger receipt

Station ladders end on a whole row above the tab rail: fold+pad paired on market rail and industry list, missions board fold retired where its snap ends whole (landed+refined by the ORRERY lane as 742cc8ebf97; pin added)
A kill that ricochets off the player's own shove now records a Thrown-wreck deed and a surviving wingmate names the physics on the bark channel
Undocked flight now hears the nearest station swell in as you close — the place sounds like a place before you reach the ring
Throwing an impulse charge now sounds its approach: throw whoosh, host bite, arm tick — the detonation stays the only boom
A quiet bar and an empty log tape now tell the player why they are empty and what writes the first line, instead of one flat sentence
A squad whose commander is pinned visibly sags — wider slots, leaderless integrity, disrupted hull — and after a grace window command passes to a wing that can still steer
A freighter you saved now sends cargo later: relief cycles earn a gratuitous gift lot waiting at the captain's home dock
A crew injury answers with a warn tick and a crew death with the hull's low groan — the loss lands in the ear, not just the comms line
Creatures react to Massline vibration: a solid tether slam wakes dormant fauna, while the resonant coil keeps quiet work quiet
Standing offers now speak in the giver's registered voice — the rescued captain and the desk regular write their own lines, not the board's
A rock breaking into chunks now sounds the brittle split at the split, once per parent per tick, graded by piece count
The latch ring now names the mass and the swing verdict — heavy bodies read WON'T BUDGE before you commit the line
A late-gated yard clerk gives the starter sector a reason to matter at hour ten — the sixteenth named cast member, gated at beat 6 with walked wrecks
A dodged lethal round is on the Record now: one dodge stunt per fight window, the near miss finally rewarded
The help screen's search and chips now read as library instruments — rail field, scale-line words — instead of bordered boxes
The approach hum now leans the station's own house — Concord rests, Reach leans, Choir hangs — so whose place it is reaches the ear before the ring
A hull the pilot tosses rattles for a beat — guns cold, one mayday over the band — and a rattled reinforcement caller now calls its screen at full hull.
A wing the pilot broke and let run keeps its name on the ledger — the return encounter can bring that crew back, and the band says the name.
The crusher jaws finally bite: a hull shoved into the anvil at crumple speed takes the collision law's own damage and the pilot who aimed the shove keeps the kill.
A fresh hull wound glows in the striking weapon's own colors before it cools to burn amber, so a furball reads as who is hitting whom with what.
The exhaust glow's own color names the maneuver: boost burns white-hot, cruise leans out cooler, idle and brake are a cooling chamber, readable across a crowd.
A fresh kill burns and smokes at its breach and cools over minutes while unstamped set dressing stays cold, so the battlefield says where something just died.
The far traffic streams twinkle like live shipping lanes: every silhouette carries an anti-collision double-flash and a running light on its own phase.
When a living-world beat starts near you — the surveyor laying its probe line, a patrol pulling a hauler over — the pocket answers with one low positioned work-bell wake instead of total silence
The convoy Dione's charts always promised now forms at the relay manifest pod with its toll escort and rolls out south, and a lost escort reads the honest empty-slot line
The station's receipt line — sales, tolls, services, the PA — is readable on the market at 1280x720 instead of painting off the top of the glass
The radio now mentions the hostile wing you downed yourself: The Margin airs the receipt once, The Static roasts or toasts it by your standing.
The rock you threw keeps its speed into the next round and the room says so, instead of the buzzer parking every body you aimed
A scanned battlefield wreck reads as a history: the black box names how it died, the manifest names what it carried, and the stamp says how long it has been dead.
The shot that empties a hull now punches through with a white core and its own light, so in a furball you can tell which hit ended them.
A shield coming back online after a break breathes once through its lattice, so you can see the shell is back before the next hit lands.

A bar regular whose story advances each visit: recognition names your last exchange, the trouble beat names what changed in the live lanes or the shelf while you were out, and the relationship settles as standing earns it.
Pick off a wingman and the enemy wing visibly folds in around the gap instead of flying a phantom slot, and a replacement releasing the fold is readable
Sustained fire leaves cool, target-bound hull scars that retain their identity across a fight.
A jackal's telegraphed mine seed is placed on the drifting rock's live pose with its current velocity when the drop actually occurs.
an anonymous hull's hail answers with its painted ship name and captain instead of its job description
The exact moving aftermath wreck carries the pilot first kill into a native second collision, one replay mark and one worker comms receipt
Released station window and berth-light surfaces retain their authored emission on the dark side without new geometry or point lights
Docking at a station you berthed at before reads one keeper line — days since your last visit — derived from the persisted dock-provenance stamps, never from feed knowledge
A berth with nothing happening reads one honest quiet line — whether its boards moved since you last read them — instead of a dead card
A dying ship's exhaust now says so: the bell cools toward ember and sputters on its own phase as the hull fails, from the same hull truth the smoke trail reads
A losing raider squad spoofs the law's own band, a Concord patrol and a Meridian screen open fire on each other through the ordinary hostility oracle, and a scanner pulse on the raider burns the lie
A marked Crucible elite kills its drive inside a room current and the field law physically carries it around the seam - one hit knocks it off the current
A lost wingman's seat says his name on the band, presses his killer for one bounded window, and a lost mining watch is named instead of silently dying
The smoke a wounded ship trails rises from the wounds it actually has, and a fresh energy wound vents the striking weapon's tint before it greys
Latching a shielded hull bites the membrane at hit parity, a strained line keeps the lattice lit while it carries the load, and a break lands one last bite
Docked, the station PA finally airs what its own market just did - a shortage or a watch-scale move over the desk chime - instead of bells and berth lanes only.
The claim buoy you paid for says it is alive - a working pulse while it holds the zone and a fast double-flash when its lease is nearly up
A scanned wreck names the captain and painted ship the registry gave it - the wreck history finally includes the person, not just the hull, cargo and time.
After selling the freight you took off the hauler you downed, the destination's price why-tip names your own kill as the cause instead of leaving that move a mystery.
Kill debris torn from a fresh named wound starts glowing in that wound's heated-metal tint and cools to the authored dark metal - the wreck field remembers what killed it for a beat
A hull a mine, charge, cookoff or the crusher jaws took now reads MINED/MILLED on the kill popup and pays the documented physics rate, instead of reading as a gun kill.
A marked elite swings until a rock sits between it and you, then holds and coasts its orbit there — flank it, hit it, and it closes again.
A hull the burn or tar corroded down now reads WASTED on the kill popup in every arena's own language, instead of reading as a gun kill.
A docking station now says where its dock is and whether it is open: gate pair, inbound lane walk and threshold bar in the cradle's own holo green, readable two rings out
A burning drive stirs the dust off the surface it hangs over: a hover over a rock or a station deck breathes dust downrange along the exhaust, following throttle and height

A lasting hull scar now points the way the shot was travelling: grazing fire smears the mark downrange while dead-center strikes keep the round blast seat, so the picture says which side got hit and how
A hull you keep hitting in the same place grows a real wound there: the seat widens, reheats under continued fire and creeps along the fire path, instead of scattering identical pocks

A patrol that acquires your standing heat no longer plays dead: it cuts its route, holds a standoff ring off your beam, and names the sheet on the band once per episode - before any scan cone or seeded hunter.

The law desk's fine card finally says what the fine is made of - the law's own base plus one step per heat band, your live step named - and what it answers for, traced through the same no-false-witness helper as the flight alert.

The after-action sheet names the situation you died in: when the hunt was live it reads the wanted band, the escape clock, and the convicting incident it traced to - instead of a bare 'Destroyed by patrol'.
A marked Crucible elite dives THROUGH a gravity well to reach you — full thrust bent through the pull, guns live — instead of holding behind a rock; a hit breaks the commit.
Shoving an enemy mine fence with your own plow now turns it into your grenade - it trips on the pack that laid it, pays your credit, and the band tells you the shove took.
The Orbital Lance now paints and strikes exactly where your crosshair points instead of a quarter-turn off it, and the thrown decoy drops ahead of the nose line.
A fresh wing dropping into your fight now reads as an arrival: faction-tinted flash, inbound lane wake and brake flare at the drop point, instead of a silent generic pop-in.
A paying wreck wears a slow amber salvage work-lamp and a stripped husk goes dark, so a furball's aftermath tells you which hulk is worth stopping for.
A docking station's apron now runs warm sodium work lights - rig pair at the dock mouth, taxi pools on the deck, a lit pad over the berth - that step up while a corridor works and hold while berthed.
A pod your magnet field takes now shows the same teal capture beat as a net catch, riding the pod from first pull — a furball catch reads on the glass
Leaving through a gate finally has a stage: the aperture swells, runs hot through the tunnel, and collapses behind your hull instead of idling for 1.2 seconds.
A survivor pod from a killed crew is now an ejection lifeboat with a distress lamp that pants harder as its oxygen drains, instead of looking like every cargo canister.
When a crew dies and its pod ejects, the moment now flashes on screen - retro burn, cold vent, and the red beacon star pulling you toward the rescue - instead of only playing a voice line.
A rich drop now announces itself - hotter glint, brighter ring, a second band - while junk chunks sit dim, so you can finally see which pod is worth chasing.
A NEW title you earn is named by the keeper at your next dock — once, in the earn verb's own flavor
The yard answers its own verbs: a paid order is stamped taken, the decant pours, and a refused decant refuses out loud instead of clicking like an info toast
The Decant key names the fuel it will move before you press it - and names which refusal is coming when the pour is unreachable

Kill every sac before it births and the room stops paying crowd cost for nobody: the cut tide is named, the done gate closes, and the emptied Hive rests instead of grinding the swarm engine to the refit.
A kill into the swarm is a kill the room notices: the linked web flinches and the neighbors sag toward the corpse - the authored BLOOM cascade finally runs instead of sitting dormant in data.

Flying the dock lane too hot no longer fades the pad to a whisper: it holds visible in caution amber, the acquisition sweep and chevron march read your own closing speed, and a settled berth calms them.
The dust sheet now rides a sector-keyed wind — the belts run brisk dusty weather, the core a near-still drift — so the vacuum reads alive and the sky says where you are even when you sit still.
Crossing into a hazard storm now plays a charge beat on your hull keyed to how hard the zone bites, and riding it keeps a family-hued static crawling the hull instead of dying invisibly.
Hazard zones now have a visible storm skin — counter-rotating ring arcs and orbiting motes in the family hue — whose density rides the live intensity, so the post-boss thinned burn reads on screen.

The pod you tow home talks: a grip on the latch, the air clock read aloud once per threshold, silence the moment the cable lets go - each line voiced on the real arbiter floor in the victim's faction register

A hauler whose drive you shot out confesses on the band - what failed and where it is adrift - while it is still a person with a problem, instead of going silent between the hit and the posthumous distress

A finished contract now names the standing it bought - '+15 MERIDIAN standing' on the completion toast and the payer's own debrief note - read back from factions' applied receipt, so softened and sealed moves stay honest and no receipt claims nothing
Bursting a Hive sac now answers: the brood it was feeding mourn around the corpse through the authored grief loop, and the combat net names the tide law once — the sacs are the room's win lever.
A big body dying now breaks the pack like one animal: seeded scatter away from the corpse, then the knot re-forms tight — the authored best throw of the fight finally runs.

The authored second pass of the bank opening no longer dies of room noise: the staged charger holds its beat while the room mourns around it, instead of walking into the hull scrum and dying before its stage calls it.

A brood bomb's death blast finally reads on the glass: the engine's swarm:broodBurst receipt was never consumed, so a cyst burst or volatile pop shoved the pack and chipped the hull without a pixel of answer — now flash, vent, star and a reach-keyed beat light wear the family's own hue.

A burst Hive sac now dies as Hive meat: the room's win lever used to die an anonymous rock's death in the default ore colour — the shatter light and two-beat burst now wear the Hive's own acid green, keyed to the hiveSac tag the room already stamps.

The brood's coupling web finally reads while a cascade is live: panic flares the pack hot acid green with a staggered urgent pulse, grief sinks it to a mourning slate — keyed to the view.cascade kind the engine already publishes, which the data contract says the renderer should flush on.

The pod you jettison reads as yours-just-lost: a hot parting beat eases into a steady claim burn on its transponder for the pickup-embargo window, then relaxes to the anonymous read exactly when the sim makes the pod public — the picture no longer contradicts the embargo.
A hired tug now speaks its own two milestones — the hook and the delivery — instead of a fee and a silent cable drag
Docking into a faction at war, the desk now names the rival — the same conflict truth the chart's war front renders, spoken by the house itself

The station that receives a towed rescue pod answers the delivery once - a bunk offered, the debt named - and an ambulance crew answers a player handoff, in the receiver's faction register on the tow voice's arbiter seam
A war the player leaned on now files a dated page in the Ship's Ledger - the front, the houses, the turn - while NPC-only flips and pre-stamp saves file nothing
The standing register now reads every deed back as words - mayday answered, fled the border, choir offering - instead of printing raw reason ids for half the things you did
A hit on the brood's relay node turns the whole flood on you — the last authored BLOOM cascade finally runs
The brood's held-back second breath names its count and bearing as it lands
The tactical AI's per-tick universe walks ride the index lanes — the crowd sim sheds a third of a millisecond a tick and grows cleaner as sectors clutter
Shoot the Queen and the pack rushes you burning red — the authored filaments-flush-red read, no longer motion-only
Leaving the storm sheds one last flicker of its hue off your hull — the exit no longer reads as someone switching the storm off
Open the throttle in the belt and your hull combs a dust wake off the drift sheet, shearing away downwind with the weather
Ride the tunnel out the far side and the gate you emerged from rebounds — discharge rings shedding off the throat instead of silent set dressing
Sitting at the bar of a house at war no longer lies that things are quiet: the conversation names the rival, the contested front, and your banked lean, on its tags and its rumors days
A returned save slot card now reads who you were: the strongest house and rung the run earned, and the war that was still burning when you filed it
Filing your ending now names the war that never cooled - the houses, the front lane, and which way your own work banked it
a rock, hull or kill-wreck you hurl through a mine fence sets off the mine it strikes; the layer's own wingman thrown into its fence is your kill
a brood wipe that opens a chain now counts every body it killed instead of one, without throwing dozens of broken-chain receipts
the chain's triple-rate guns at the score cap are named when they open and when the break takes them away, with their own chime and dip
a rock you throw through a mine fence lights the contact that set it off - the strike reads in the custody's own hue keyed to the throw, and a field-turned mine claims your side on the glass
the wreck you scan answers at the hull - the pulse lands on it and a quiet scanner-blue lamp holds it findable for the ping window instead of leaving it anonymous in the field
the crusher's verdict reads at the anvil - a steel crumple pop along your shove, sparks off the contact, and a kill star when the jaws empty a hull, instead of another anonymous hit flash
a ghost contact snaps into a real ship under your last pulse, and the one you failed to hold melts away at its last known position - the deception loop finally reads both ways

Docking after a week of war now cites the war itself: the weekly digest's fact pool hears a front boiling over and a front resolving, so the world's own biggest story reaches the dock line instead of only your deeds.

The moment a rescued pod crosses the ring, the receiving berth answers with its own authored chime - a struck bell with an answering fifth - instead of silence, so the delivery sounds like a place taking someone in and not like your hull bumping the dock.

A war that ends no longer vanishes into silence: for three sim days after the front resolves, docking at either house names the peace - who took the lane, from whom - straight off the conflict record's own flip stamp, instead of the war going quiet like it never happened.
